info.title: TiDB Link Customer API
info.description: Customer integration API at /api/v1. Operations declare End User API Key, Organization API Key or ticket authorization. Old customer addresses have been removed without aliases; existing SDKs and external callers require a separate migration.

parameters.name: cursor

200.description: A persisted Server-Sent Events stream under current User Key, ordinary User, and Organization authority. Revocation, rotation, or disabling the User or Organization closes the subscription. The cursor in each id field can be supplied on a later request. Disconnecting the subscription does not cancel the active Turn. Each data frame is a JSON envelope with type, sessionId, turnId, createdAt and data. Turn events (agent.session.turn.*) carry the durable Turn event in data. Realtime facts of the Session timeline arrive in the same order: agent.session.realtime.input_transcript.completed for each final user transcript and agent.session.realtime.response.completed for each completed Realtime model response, with data {id, type, realtimeConnectionId, text, turnId, createdAt} and, for a response, kind (chat, task_ack, task_progress, task_result, clarify; historical device_ack remains readable), responseId and interrupted. Their envelope turnId is the linked Turn or null. Partial Realtime transcripts are delivered only on the realtime connection. agent.session.turn.output_text.snapshot carries the complete provisional draft in data.payload.text: replace the draft for that turnId, including revisions or an empty reset, rather than appending. A resumed snapshot is independently usable without earlier draft frames. agent.session.turn.progress carries a separate progress message in data.payload.text. agent.session.turn.item.added with data.event = assistant_message carries the final saved message in data.payload.text and data.payload.messageId; the terminal Turn event establishes its outcome. agent.session.turn.item.added with data.event = operation_step carries data.payload.operationId, status and label; a tool Operation also carries data.payload.category (skill_read for a read inside a frozen Skill package, with data.payload.skill {skillId, name}; otherwise tool_call), matching the Operation in Turn reads. Client Tool progress also carries safe data.payload.source: {type: session_client} or {type: hardware, hardwareRequirementId, method}; Hardware labels identify the requirement and original method. Hardware arguments, outputs and private target identities are omitted from progress and Turn Operations. The hardware_read_state platform tool creates a hardware.state.read Operation; public input contains only its tool name and requirement identifier, and output omits sensor data. Metadata-only Operations omit source. Events saved before these fields existed omit them. agent.session.turn.requires_action with data.event = client_tool_calls carries data.payload.calls, the Client Tool calls of one model step, each with callId, name, arguments and deadlineAt; answer each with agent.session.input.client_tool_output before its deadline. Receiving this event counts as delivery of its calls. No output_text.delta alias is emitted.

200.description: An idempotent replay of an already accepted command.

202.description: The command was accepted. Message and cancellation commands return durable interaction receipts; retry commands return a retrying event receipt. Execution progress is delivered separately by GET /events.

400.description: The command envelope or command data is invalid, or an idle text Turn admission exceeds the combined Session-client and Hardware tool limit after model projection (64 tools or 64 KiB; validation_failed). Admission saves no input or Turn on this overflow. New checkpoint retries are disabled by default and return checkpoint_runtime_unavailable when disabled or unavailable; previously accepted retry commands still recover their receipts.

403.description: An active End User principal is required.

404.description: The Session is unavailable or authorization-hidden, or a client_tool_output references an unknown, foreign or Hardware call (client_tool_call_unavailable).

409.description: The command identity was already used with a different body or target state, or a new message or retry targets a read-only Session (session_read_only).

503.description: New Turn admission is temporarily closed for deployment maintenance or recovery (turn_admission_closed), or the deployment lacks the Sandbox or Drive9 service a new Turn needs (service_configuration_unavailable; details.reason names it). This refusal happens before the command is saved, so the same clientEventId can be sent again once the service is set up. If the configuration changes after that check, the command is accepted instead and its Turn fails with the same code and reason in turn_error. A model the deployment does not configure keeps its 409 model_provider_unconfigured refusal.

200.description: A bounded page of the Session timeline. Each entry is a complete Turn (messages with inputContext, Operations with category and skill, Artifact publications) or one Realtime fact: a final user transcript or a completed Realtime model response. Realtime facts follow their durable write order. A Turn started by a Realtime utterance (a task or a clarification answer) is placed directly after that utterance; every other Turn, including one a Realtime utterance only steered, sits where its first event was saved. Because that utterance is saved after the Turn starts, a client that paged past such a Turn in the meantime can see it again on a later page; nothing is skipped. Key entries by Turn id and Realtime fact id, replace an entry that arrives again, and group Realtime facts by their turnId. A running Turn is a snapshot of its progress so far; read it again or follow GET /events for later changes.

post.description: Authorization: UserApiKey; persisted credentials determine Organization and End User scope.

Admits a Realtime connection on an existing Session owned by the authenticated End User. The connection inherits the Session’s Agent and Billing Tag and freezes the Session’s selected Realtime Model and its provider identity. A null Session selection uses the release default; a withdrawn selection is refused without fallback. Changing the Session selection affects only the next connection. The response carries a first one-time connect token; mint more with POST /api/v1/user/sessions/{id}/realtime/connect-tokens. A Session has at most one live (connecting, active or paused) Realtime connection: while one exists this route answers 409 realtime_connection_live with details [{ "path": "/", "reason": "live realtime connection <id>" }]. Text and Realtime interaction may alternate on the same Session. A connection that never connects within 120 seconds, or whose server runtime stopped renewing its lease for 60 seconds, is ended automatically.

Authorization: UserApiKey; persisted credentials determine Organization and End User scope.

201.description: The admitted Realtime connection and a one-time connect token.

400.description: ErrorEnvelope code: validation_error, audio_format_unsupported.

403.description: ErrorEnvelope code: user_api_key_required. Only a User API Key is accepted; a browser Session or an Organization API Key is refused.

404.description: ErrorEnvelope code: session_not_found (missing, deleted or not owned).

409.description: ErrorEnvelope code: realtime_connection_live, session_read_only, realtime_not_enabled, realtime_language_unsupported, realtime_model_unavailable.

503.description: ErrorEnvelope code: admission_unavailable. Retry the request.

UserApiKey.description: Opaque ti_user_<id>_<secret> credential: ASCII alphanumeric id body (1–64), unpadded base64url secret (43 characters from 32 random bytes). Authenticates the bound User and Organization. The persisted key owner determines scope.

OrganizationApiKey.description: Opaque ti_org_<id>_<secret> credential: ASCII alphanumeric id body (1–64), unpadded base64url secret (43 characters from 32 random bytes). Authenticates an Organization machine principal with no acting User. Each handler explicitly chooses whether to admit this principal kind.

input.description: Kind-specific input. A tool Operation has toolName and args; a Hardware Client Tool exposes only toolName, callId and mode, omitting device arguments. Neither input nor output carries the model supplier's tool-call id; use the Operation id to identify a tool call and its result.

output.description: Kind-specific result. Hardware Client Tool Operations omit output in every status. An llm.complete Operation exposes usage as token counts only: input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens, and optional cacheWrite1h and reasoning. Counts that are unavailable or invalid are omitted; absent usage is omitted. Supplier SDK cost is not exposed. Customer fees are available from the Billing usage APIs. A failed or interrupted llm.complete Operation has error {code, message, details?} with fixed text only; model_provider_failed carries details.provider (category, httpStatus, errorType, errorCode); other failures use runtime_error or a ledger outcome code. Any other failed, interrupted or unknown_result Operation with an error, including tool Operations, has error {code, message, details} with fixed text naming only the tool: an intentional tool code (for example mcp_unavailable or validation_error) is kept; an allow-listed web_search_* or session_recall_* reason becomes the code and is repeated as details.code with a boolean details.retryable; anything else reads tool_failed. A memory.recall Operation keeps only memory_recall_failed, turn_interrupted or operation_result_unknown, and otherwise reads tool_failed. details also carries tool, category (rejected, unavailable, remote_error, failed, unknown_result, interrupted or unexpected) and, when known, dispatch and retryContract.

Output: pcm16 8000, 16000 or 24000 Hz (default), or opus 24000 Hz with packetDurationMs 20 and fixed bitrate 16000, 24000 or 32000 bps (default 32000). bitrate is accepted only on opus output.
